rollout.markets: TP-01-EPCAL in New York metro, with Phoenix – Scottsdale carried in parallel
rollout.rationale: The best MARKET and the best SITE are not the same answer. Phoenix – Scottsdale ranks first on the market screen; New York metro ranks 23 of 23. The pipeline still leads with TP-01-EPCAL because the composite scores the actual dirt — catchment, entitlement posture and infrastructure already in the ground — not the metro average, and on that basis the top two are inside a point of each other. Both go into Tranche 1 diligence and the cost basis decides. A market rank is a prior; a site is evidence.

fragility.verdict: THE RANKING HOLDS AND THE ECONOMICS DO NOT, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL ANSWER. Write the $9,500,000 site cost credit at TP-01-EPCAL down to zero and it still leads TP-06-PINAL-303 on the composite by 2.5 points — but it returns 7.4% against 9.2%, so the runner-up out-earns it by 180 basis points. The composite spends 20 of its 100 points on yield, so a swing of this size barely moves it. That credit is the reuse of existing runway pavement as base course, on a runway around which fifteen PFAS areas of concern were identified in 2023. Rank on the composite if you like; fund the one that earns more.

respec.verdict: THE COMP CASE IS A SPECIFICATION PROBLEM, NOT ONLY A PRICING ONE. At comp-supported pricing the configured programme returns -0.1% and covers at 0.88x. A 510-member club on 2.25 miles with 110 garage condos returns 13.5% and covers at 2.29x — clearing every governing test on the same dirt at the same prices. The lever is MEMBER COUNT, not track length: across the searched range track length is worth 107 bp of IRR and the for-sale count 776 bp, and the for-sale count moves the WRONG WAY — more units lower the return, because the vertical is 43% of non-land cost on a thin comp-supported margin and the carry runs until the last one sells.

bridge.verdict: No single driver reaches 15%. The best is Initiation fee +50% at 12.9% against a 8.8% base. It takes 2 of them together — Initiation fee +50% + Annual dues +25% — to reach 15.4%. That is not a base case; it is 2 independent things going right at once, and the scenario set already prices that as the upside.

rows.q: Will members pay $34,000 a year where buying real estate is optional? The comparable set's ceiling outside a mandatory-purchase club or invitation-only Miami is $18,500.
Can 340 members actually be recruited at this price? Every rate in the demand funnel — collector share, track-active share, incumbent capture — is judgment, not measured conversion.
Is the circuit and vertical hard cost right? Nothing in the package is a bid; the whole cost stack is benchmark-derived.
Is the $150,000 initiation collectable, and is any of it REFUNDABLE? The reference asset is reported to refund 70% on exit, which would make most of it a liability rather than income.
Can 23 units a year be absorbed? M1 realised 17.5 and NJMP delivered 10-15 across nine phases in fifteen years — and NJMP is the closest structural Northeast analogue there is.
Will a club operator run this at the modelled operating ratio? No operator is appointed and the ratio drives the covenant.
Will garage condominiums sell at $530/SF? The two operating new-build track comps price at $344-352 — which is this model's assumed HARD COST, before the 1.298x soft and contingency load.
Will the IDA grant a 50% PILOT? Without it the covenant breaks and maximum supportable land goes negative. Section 862 eligibility for a private recreation use is the open question.

Is the EPCAL runway pavement reusable as base course, or is it a PFAS waste-characterisation problem? The Navy identified fifteen new areas of concern around that runway in 2023, sourced to firefighting foam.
Does the Northeast initiation ceiling of $125,000 hold? It rests on ONE AI-generated wiki entry about ONE club, with a five-fold gap to the next observation in the set.
Will a 7.25% exit cap clear for a special-purpose recreational asset with a thin buyer universe?
Is the site infrastructure budget real? Earthwork, utilities and stormwater are carried at benchmark on a parcel nobody has surveyed.
Is 210 usable days right for the lead site? The only published Northeast facility figure in the comp set is 150 days, at a materially colder site.
How long is the entitlement path really, and what does running it cost? The researched path at the lead site is 45 months against the programme's 33, and fourteen of fifteen sites revised up.
What is the daytime dBA limit at the nine sites where none is published? Two have ordinances whose tables would not open; seven publish nothing.
What does large-acreage land actually trade at in the target counties, and who owns these parcels? No land comparables were obtained and no target carries an APN, coordinates or an owner to call.
Is the EPCAL disposition free to transact? In litigation since 2024, one cause of action surviving dismissal in February 2026, land described as in limbo throughout.
Does the circuit meet the municipal standard at the property line, as designed? A fail here is not a cost line — it is a redesign, a berm programme, or a different site.

Do 4.0 miles of circuit, 140 garage condominiums and the homesites fit the parcel at a workable grade? The re-specification search wants a shorter course; nobody has drawn either version on real topography.
rows.rng: fits as drawn, or the programme changes

rows.q: Can both finalists be optioned, at what price, and for long enough to run the entitlement? Nothing is under contract and one of the two is in litigation over its disposition.

listing.verdict: NOT LISTABLE BY YEAR 10 ON EITHER ROUTE. 5 stabilised assets are needed. Ground-up reaches that in year 22; even an acquisition-led platform reaches it in year 12. Year 10 is when club 1 finishes ramping, not when a platform lists. The earliest credible route is acquisition-led at year 12; treat a listing as a year-12 stretch outcome, plan the platform for it, and underwrite to a strategic sale or recapitalisation in the meantime.

exits.requires: Delivery and absorption only — no capital-markets event
exits.assessment: HIGHEST CERTAINTY. Returns the majority of invested capital independent of any exit market. This is why the programme is structured as a merchant build.
HIGH CERTAINTY once the club is credible. Collected as the club fills and never repaid.

exits.basis: Permanent debt sized on stabilised NOI
exits.requires: Stabilised operating history and covenant compliance
exits.assessment: PROBABLE. Note the negative-leverage finding: refinancing is a liquidity tool here, not a return enhancer, and should not be sized to the maximum available.

exits.route: Strategic sale of the retained club
exits.requires: A buyer for single-asset special-purpose recreational property
exits.assessment: REALISTIC BUT THIN. Buyer universe is family offices, club operators and member-buyout vehicles, not institutional core capital. Break-even cap is 8.95%; beyond that the club is worth less than it cost to keep.

exits.basis: $113M of club financing capacity plus a $184,849 per-member assessment to reach the exit-cap value
exits.requires: A cohesive, capitalised membership willing to assess itself
exits.assessment: The standard end-state for private clubs, and now priced rather than asserted. PLAUSIBLE BUT NOT A FLOOR. Financing capacity is $113M against a $176M exit-cap value; closing the gap costs each member $184,849, roughly 1.2 initiation fees. Expect a negotiated price below the cap-rate valuation.

exits.assessment: PLAUSIBLE IF THE PLATFORM IS BUILT. Requires the second and third clubs, which requires club 1 to prove the model first.

Ground-up reaches that in year 22; even an acquisition-led platform reaches it in year 12. Year 10 is when club 1 finishes ramping, not when a platform lists. The earliest credible route is acquisition-led at year 12; treat a listing as a year-12 stretch outcome, plan the platform for it, and underwrite to a strategic sale or recapitalisation in the meantime.
